O Indra-Varuṇa, ours be this treasure ours be wealth, Maruts, with full store of heroes. May the Varûtrîs with their shelter aid us, and Bhâratî and Hotrâ with the Mornings.
translation.context: From Mandala 3, Sukta 62 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Agni
translation.summary: , Thee Agni, have the Gods, ever of one accord, sent hither down, a God, appointed messenger, yea, with their wisdom sent thee down.
verses: , THEE Agni, have the Gods, ever of one accord, sent hither down, a God, appointed messenger, yea, with their wisdom sent thee down. The Immortal, O thou Holy One, mid mortal men, the God-devoted God, the wise, have they brought forth, brought forth the omnipresent God-devoted Sage.
As such, O Agni, bring with favour to the Gods thy Brother Varuṇa who loveth sacrifice, True to the Law, the Âditya who supporteth men, the King, supporter of mankind.

Do thou, O Friend, turn hither him who is our Friend, swift as a wheel, like two car-steeds in rapid course, Wondrous! to us in rapid course. O Agni, find thou grace for us with Varuṇa, with Maruts who illumine all. Bless us, thou Radiant One, for seed and progeny, yea, bless us, O thou Wondrous God.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 1 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacrifice to Agni
translation.summary: The, Faithful One, Immortal among mortals, a God among the Gods, appointed envoy, Priest, best at worship, must shine forth in glory .
verses: THE, Faithful One, Immortal among mortals, a God among the Gods, appointed envoy, Priest, best at worship, must shine forth in glory . Agni shall be raised high with man's oblations.
Born for us here this day, O Son of Vigour, between both races of born beings, Agni, Thou farest as an envoy, having harnessed, Sublime One! thy strong-muscled radiant stallions.
I laud the ruddy steeds who pour down blessing, dropping oil, flectest through the thoualit of Order. Yoking red horses to and fro thou goest between you Deities and mortal races.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 2 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Offering to Agni
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: WIN, to assist you, Rudra, Lord of worship, Priest of both worlds, effectual Sacrificer, Agni, invested with his golden colours, before the thunder strike and lay you senseless.
This shrine have we made ready for thy coming, as the fond dame attires her for her husband. Performer of good work, sit down before us, invested while these flames incline to meet thee.
A hymn, O Priest, to him who hears, the gentle, to him who looks on men, exceeding gracious, A song of praise sing to the God Immortal, whom the stone, presser of the sweet juice, worships.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 3 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Put forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour; go like a mighty
translation.summary: Put forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour; go like a mighty King with his attendants.
verses: PUT forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour; go like a mighty King with his attendants. Thou, following thy swift net, shootest arrows: transfix the fiends with darts that burn most fiercely.
Forth go in rapid flight thy whirling weapons: follow them closely, glowing in thy fury. Spread with thy tongue the winged flames, O Agni; unfettered, cast thy firebrands all around thee.
Send thy spies forward, flectest in thy motion; be, ne'er deceived, the guardian of this people From him who, near or far, is bent on evil, and let no trouble sent from thee o'ercome us.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 4 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni's Brilliance
translation.summary: How shall we give with one accord oblation to Agni, to Vaiṣvânara the Bounteous.
verses: How shall we give with one accord oblation to Agni, to Vaiṣvânara the Bounteous? Great light, with full high growth hath he uplifted, and, as a pillar bears the roof, sustains it.
Reproach not him who, God and selfreliant, vouchsafed this bounty unto me a mortal,– Deathless, discerner, wise, to me the simple, Vaiṣvânara most manly, youthful Aini.
Sharp-pointed, powerful, strong, of boundless vigour, Agni who knows the lofty hymn, kept secret As the lost milch-cow's track, the doubly Mighty,– he hath declared to me this hidden knowledge.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 5 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacrifice to Agni
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: PRIEST of our rite, stand up erect, O Agni, in the Gods' service best of sacrificers, For over evei y thought thou art the Ruler: thou furtherest e'en the wisdom of the pious.
He was set down mid men as Priest unerring, Agni, wise, welcome in our holy synods. Like Savitar he hath lifted up his splendour, and like a builder raised his smoke to heaven.
The glowing ladle, filled with oil, is lifted; choosing Gods' service to the right he circles. Eager he rises like the new-wrought pillar which, firmly set and fixed, anoints the victims.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 6 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Here by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker
translation.summary: A sacred hymn from the ancient Rigveda.
verses: HERE by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites: Whom Apnavâna, and the Bhr̥igus caused to shine bright-coloured in the wood, spreading from home to home.
When shall thy glory as a God, Agni, be suddenly shown forth. For mortal men have held thee fast, adorable in all their homes,
Seeing thee faithful to the Law, most sapient, like the starry heaven, Illumining with cheerful ray each solemn rite in every house.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 7 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Your envoy who possesses all
translation.summary: Your envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts, Best worshipper, I woo with song..
verses: YOUR envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts, Best worshipper, I woo with song.
He, Mighty, knows the gift of wealth, he knows the deep recess of heaven: He shall bring hitherward the Gods.
He knows, a God himself, to guide Gods to the righteous in his home: He gives e'en treasures that we love.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 8 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Agni
translation.summary: Agni, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come, To seat thee on the sacred grass..
verses: AGNI, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come, To seat thee on the sacred grass.
May he the Immortal, Helper, bard to be deceived among mankind, Become the messenger of all.
Around the altar is he led, welcome Chief Priest at solemn rites, Or as the Potar sits him down.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 9 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Agni
translation.summary: This day with praises, Agni, we bring thee that which thou lovest. Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions..
verses: This day with praises, Agni, we bring thee that which thou lovest. Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions.
For thou hast ever been the Car-driver, Agni, of noble Strength, lofty sacrifice, and rightful judgment.
Through these our praises come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight, O Agni, well disposed, with all thine aspects.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 10 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni the Divine
translation.summary: Thy blessed majesty, victorious Agni, shines brightly in the neighbourhood of Sûrya.
verses: THY blessed majesty, victorious Agni, shines brightly in the neighbourhood of Sûrya. Splendid to see, it shows even at nighttime, and food is fair to look on in thy beauty.

Agni, disclose his thought for him who singeth, the well, Strong God! while thou art praised with fervour. Vouchsafe to us that powerful hymn, O Mighty, which, Radiant One! with all the Gods thou lovest.
From thee, O Agni, springs poetic wisdom, from thee come thoughts and hymns of praise that prosper; From thee flows wealth, with heroes to adorn it, to the true-hearted man who gives oblation.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 11 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Strength of Agni
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: WHOSO enkindles thee, with lifted ladle, and thrice this day offers thee food, O Agni, May he excel, triumphant through thy splendours, wise through thy mental power, O Jâtavedas.
Whoso with toil and trouble brings thee fuel, serving the majesty of mighty Agni, He, kindling thee at evening and at morning, prospers, and comes to wealth, and slays his foemen.
Agni is Master of sublime dominion, Agni is Lord of strength and lofty riches. Straightway the self-reliant God, Most Youthful, gives treasures to the mortal who adores him.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 12 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Wealth from Agni
translation.summary: Agni hath looked, benevolently-minded, on the wealth-giving spring of radiant Mornings.
verses: AGNI hath looked, benevolently-minded, on the wealth-giving spring of radiant Mornings. Come, Aṣvins, to the dwelling of the pious: Sûrya the God is rising with his splendour.
Savitar, God, hath spread on high his lustre, waving his flag like a spoil-seeking hero. Their stablished way go Varuṇa and Mitra, what time they make the Sun ascend the heaven.
Him whom they made to drive away the darkness, Lords of sure mansions, constant to their object, Him who beholds the universe, the Sun-God, seven strong and youthful Coursers carry onward.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 13 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacrifice to Agni
translation.summary: The God hath looked, even Agni Jâtavedas, to meet the Dawns refulgent in their glories.
verses: THE God hath looked, even Agni Jâtavedas, to meet the Dawns refulgent in their glories. Come on your chariot, ye who travel widely, come to this sacrifice of ours, Nâsatyas.
Producing light for all the world of creatures, God Savitar hath raised aloft his banner. Making his presence known by sunbeams, Sûrya hath filled the firmament and earth and heaven.
Red Dawn.is come, riding with brightness onward, distinguished by her beams, gay-hued and mighty. Dawn on her nobly-harnessed car, the Goddess, awaking men to happiness, approacheth.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 14 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Agni
translation.summary: Agni the Herald, like a horse, is led forth at our solemn rite, God among Gods adorable..
verses: AGNI the Herald, like a horse, is led forth at our solemn rite, God among Gods adorable.
Three times unto our solemn rite comes Agni like a charioteer, Bearing the viands to the Gods.
Round the oblations hath he paced, Agni the Wise, the Lord of Strength, Giving the offerer precious boons.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 15 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 4.16
translation.summary: Impetuous, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his Tawny Coursers speed to reach us.
verses: IMPETUOUS, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his Tawny Coursers speed to reach us. For him have we pressed juice exceeding potent: here, praised with song, let him effect his visit.
Unyoke, as at thy journey's end, O Hero, to gladden thee today at this libation. Like Uṣanâ, the priest a laud shall utter, a hymn to thee, the Lord Divine, who markest.
When the Bull, quaffing, praises our Iibation, as a sage paying holy rites in secret, Seven singers here from heaven hath he begotten, who e'en by day have wrought their works while singing.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 16 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Indra
translation.summary: Great art thou, Indra; yea, the earth, with gladness, and heaven confess to thee thine high dominion.
verses: GREAT art thou, Indra; yea, the earth, with gladness, and heaven confess to thee thine high dominion. Thou in thy vigour having slaughtered Vr̥itra didst free the floods arrested by the Dragon.
Heaven trembled at the birth of thine effulgence; Earth trembled at the fear of thy displeasure. The stedfast mountains shook in agitation . the waters flowed, and desert spots were flooded.

Hurling his bolt with might he cleft the mountain, while, putting forth his strength, he showed his vigour. He slaughtered Vr̥itra with his bolt, exulting, and, their lord slain, forth flowed the waters swiftly.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 17 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: This is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have c
translation.summary: This is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have come into existence. Hereby could one be born though waxen mighty.
verses: THIS is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have come into existence. Hereby could one be born though waxen mighty. Let him not, otherwise, destroy his Mother.
Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue. Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question.
He bent his eye upon the dying Mother: My word I now withdraw. That way I follow. In Tvashṭar's dwelling India drank the Soma, a hundredworth of juice pressed from the mortar.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 18 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra's Power
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: THEE, verily, O Thunder-wielding Indra, all the Gods here, the Helpers swift to listen, And both the worlds elected, thee the Mighty, High, waxen strong, alone to slaughter Vr̥itra.
The Gods, as worn witheld, relaxed their efforts: thou, Indra, born of truth, wast Sovran Ruler. Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and duggest out their all-supporting channels.
The insatiate one, extended, hard to waken, who slumbered in perpetual sleep, O Indra,– The Dragon stretched against the seven prone rivers, where no joint was, thou rentest with thy thunder.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 19 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra the Mighty
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: FROM near or far away may mighty Indra giver of succour, come for our protection Lord of men, armed with thunder, with the Strongest, slaying his foes in conflict, in the battles.
May Indra come to us with Tawny Coursers, inclined to us, to favour and enrich us. May Maghavan, loud-voiced and wielding thunder, stand by us at this sacrifice, in combat.
Thou, honouring this our sacrifice, O Indra, shalt give us strength and fill us full of courage. To win the booty, Thunder-armed! like hunters may we with thee subdue in fight our foemen.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 20 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Indra
translation.summary: May Indra come to us for our protection; here be the Hero, praised, our feast-companion.
verses: MAY Indra come to us for our protection; here be the Hero, praised, our feast-companion. May he whose powers are many, waxen mighty, cherish, like Dyaus, his own supreme dominion.
Here magnify his great heroic exploits, most glorious One, enriching men with bounties, Whose will is like a Sovran in assembly, who rules the people, Conqueror, all-surpassing.
Hither let Indra come from earth or heaven, hither with speech from firmament or ocean; With Maruts, from the realm of light to aid us, or from a distance, from the seat of Order.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 21 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Indra
translation.summary: That gift of ours which Indra loves and welcomes, even that he makes for us, the Great and Strong One.
verses: THAT gift of ours which Indra loves and welcomes, even that he makes for us, the Great and Strong One. He who comes wielding in his might the thunder, Maghavan, gives prayer, praise, and laud, and Soma.
Bull, hurler of the four-edged rain-producer with both his arms, strong, mighty, most heroic; Wearing as wool Parushṇî for adornment, whose joints for sake of friendship he hath covered.
God who of all the Gods was born divinest, endowed with ample strength and mighty powers, And bearing in his arrns the yearning thunder, with violent rush caused heaven and earth to tremble.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 22 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Wealth from Soma
translation.summary: How, what priest's sacrifice hath he made mighty, rejoicing in the Soma and its fountain.
verses: How, what priest's sacrifice hath he made mighty, rejoicing in the Soma and its fountain? Delighting in juice, eagerly drinking, the Lofty One hath waxed for splendid riches.
What hero hath been made his feast-companion? Who hath been partner in his loving-kindness? What know we of his wondrous acts? How often comes he to aid and speed the pious toiler?
How heareth Indra offered invocation? How, hearing, marketh he the invoker's wishes? What are his ancient acts of bounty? Wherefore call they him One who filleth full the singer?
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 23 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Indra
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: WHAT worthy praise will bring before us Indra, the Son of Strength, that he may grant us riches; For he the Hero, gives the singer treasures: he is the Lord who sends us gifts, ye people.
To be invoked and hymned in fight with Vr̥itra, that well-praised Indra gives us real bounties. That Maghavan brings comfort in the foray to the religious man who pours libations.
Him, verily, the men invoke in combat; risking their lives they make him their protector, When heroes, foe to foe, give up their bodies, fighting, each side, for children and their offspring.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 24 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Indra
translation.summary: What friend of man, God-loving, hath delighted, yearning therefor, this day in Indra's friendship.
verses: WHAT friend of man, God-loving, hath delighted, yearning therefor, this day in Indra's friendship? Who with enkindled flame and flowing Soma laudeth him for his great protecting favour?
Who hath with prayer bowed to the Soma-lover? What pious man endues the beams of morning? Who seeks bond, fritridship, brotherhood with Indra? Who hath recourse unto the Sage for succour?
Who claims to-day the Deities' protection, asks Aditi for light, or the Âdityas? Of whose pressed stalk of Soma drink the Aṣvins, Indra, and Agni, well-inclined in spirit?
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 25 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Prayer to Sūrya
translation.summary: I Was aforetime Manu, I was Sûrya: I am the sage Kakshîvân, holy singer. Kutsa the son of Arjuni I master. I am the sapient Uṣanâ behold me..
verses: I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Sûrya: I am the sage Kakshîvân, holy singer. Kutsa the son of Arjuni I master. I am the sapient Uṣanâ behold me.
I have bestowed the earth upon the Ârya, and rain upon the man who brings oblation. I guided forth the loudly-roaring waters, and the Gods moved according to my pleasure.
In the wild joy of Soma I demolished Ṣambara's forts, ninety-and-nine, together; And, utterly, the hundredth habitation, when helping Divodâsa Âtithigva.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 26 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 4.27
translation.summary: I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order.
verses: I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order. A hundred iron fortresses confined me but forth I flew with rapid speed a Falcon.
Not at his own free pleasure did he bear me: he conquered with his strength and manly courage. Straightway the Bold One left the fiends behind him and passed the winds as he grew yet more mighty.
When with loud cry from heaven down sped the Falcon, thence hasting like the wind he bore the Bold One. Then, wildly raging in his mind, the archer Kr̥iṣanu aimed and loosed the string to strike him.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 27 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Indra
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: ALLIED with thee, in this thy friendship, Soma, Indra for man made waters flow together, Slew Ahi, and sent forth the Seven Rivers, and opened as it were obstructed fountains.
Indu, with thee for his confederate, Indra swiftly with might pressed down the wheel of Sûrya. What rolled, all life's support, on heaven's high summit was separated from the great oppressor.
Indra smote down, Agni consumed, O Indu, the Dasyus ere the noontide in the conflict. Of those who gladly sought a hard-won dwelling he cast down many a thousand with his arrow.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 28 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Indra
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: COME, lauded, unto us with powers and succours, O Indra, with thy Tawny Steeds; exulting, Past even the foeman's manifold libations, glorified with our hymns, true Wealth-bestower.
Man's Friend, to this our sacrifice he cometh marking how he is called by Soma-pressers. Fearless, and conscious that his Steeds are noble, he joyeth with the Soma-pouring heroes.
Make his cars hear, that he may show his vigour and may be joyful in the way he loveth. May mighty Indra pouring forth in bounty bestow on us good roads and perfect safety;
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 29 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Prayer to Indra
translation.summary: O Indra, Vr̥itra-slayer, none is better, mightier than thou: Verily there is none like thee..
verses: O INDRA, Vr̥itra-slayer, none is better, mightier than thou: Verily there is none like thee.
Like chariot-wheels these people all together follow after thee: Thou ever art renowned as Great.
Not even all the gathered Gods conquered thee, Indra, in the war, When thou didst lengthen days by night.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 30 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: What help will he come to us
translation.summary: With what help will he come to us, wonderful, ever-waxing Friend; With what most mighty company?.
verses: WITH what help will he come to us, wonderful, ever-waxing Friend; With what most mighty company?
What genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst Open e'en strongly-guarded wealth?
Do thou who art Protector of us thy friends who praise thee With hundred aids approach us.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 31 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra's Power
translation.summary: O Thou who slewest Vr̥itra, come, O Indra, hither to our side, Mighty One with thy mighty aids..
verses: O THOU who slewest Vr̥itra, come, O Indra, hither to our side, Mighty One with thy mighty aids.
Swift and impetuous art thou, wondrous amid the well-dressed folk: Thou doest marvels for our help.
Even with the weak thou smitest down him who is stronger, with thy strength The mighty, with the Friends thou hast.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 32 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Sacred Cattle
translation.summary: I Send my voice as herald to the R̥ibhus; I crave the white cow for the overspreading.
verses: I SEND my voice as herald to the R̥ibhus; I crave the white cow for the overspreading. Wind-sped, the Skillful Ones in rapid motion have in an instant compassed round the heaven.
What time the Rbus had with care and marvels done proper service to assist their Parents, They won the friendship of the Gods; the Sages carried away the fruit of their devotion.
May they who made their Parents, who were lying like posts that moulder, young again for ever,– May Vâja, Vibhvan, R̥ibhu, joined with Indra , protect our sacrifice, the Soma-lovers.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 33 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra the Bestower of Wealth
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: To this our sacrifice come R̥ibhu, Vibhvan, Vâja, and Indra with the gift of riches, Because this day hath Dhishaṇâ the Goddess set drink for you: the gladdening draughts have reached you.
Knowing your birth and rich in gathered treasure, R̥ibhus, rejoice together with the Rtus. The gladdening draughts and wisdom have approached you: send ye us riches with good store of heroes.
For you was made this sacrifice, O R̥ibhus, which ye, like men, won for yourselves aforetime. To you come all who find in you their pleasure: ye all were-even the two elder-Vâjas.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 34 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra's Treasures
translation.summary: Come hither, O ye Sons of Strength, ye R̥ibhus; stay not afar, ye Children of Sudhanvan. At this libation is your gift of treasure.
verses: Come hither, O ye Sons of Strength, ye R̥ibhus; stay not afar, ye Children of Sudhanvan. At this libation is your gift of treasure. Let gladdening draughts approach you after Indra's.
Hither is come the R̥ibhus' gift of riches; here was the drinking of the well-pressed Soma, Since by dexterity and skill as craftsmen ye made the single chalice to be fourfold
Ye made fourfold the chalice that wag single: ye spake these words and said, O Friend, assist us; Then, Vâjas! gained the path of life eternal, deft-handed R̥ibhus, to the Gods' assembly.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 35 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Divine Steed
translation.summary: THia car that was not made for horses or for reins, three-wheeled, worthy of lauds, rolls round the firmament.
verses: THia car that was not made for horses or for reins, three-wheeled, worthy of lauds, rolls round the firmament. That is the great announcement of your Deity, that, O ye R̥ibhus, ye sustain the earth and heaven.
Ye Sapient Ones who made the lightly-rolling car out of your mind, by thought, the car that never errs, You, being such, to drink of this drinkoffering, you, O ye Vâjas, and ye R̥ibhus, we invoke.
O Vâjas, R̥ibhus, reaching far, among the Gods this was your exaltation gloriously declared, In that your aged Parents, worn with length of days, ye wrought again to youth so that they moved at will.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 36 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Come to our sacrifice
translation.summary: A sacred hymn from the ancient Rigveda.
verses: COME to our sacrifice, Vâjas, R̥ibhukshans, Gods, by the paths which Gods are wont to travel, As ye, gay Gods, accept in splendid weather the sacrifice among these folk of Manus.
May these rites please you in your heart and spirit; may the drops clothed in oil this day approach you. May the abundant juices bear you onward to power and strength, and, when imbibed, delight you.
Your threefold going near is God-appointed, so praise is given you, Vâjas and R̥ibhukshans. So, Manus-like, mid younger folk I offer, to you who are aloft in heaven, the Soma.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 37 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: You two came the gifts in days aforetime which Trasadasyu granted
translation.summary: From you two came the gifts in days aforetime which Trasadasyu granted to the Pûrus.
verses: FROM you two came the gifts in days aforetime which Trasadasyu granted to the Pûrus. Ye gave the winner of our fields and plough-lands, and the strong smiter who subdued the Dasytis.
And ye gave mighty Dadhikrâs, the giver of many gifts, who visiteth all people, Impetuous hawk, swift and of varied colour, like a brave King whom each true man must honour.
Whom, as 'twere down a precipice, swift rushing, each Pûru praises and his heart rejoices,– Springing forth like a hero fain for battle, whirling the car and flying like the tempest.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 38 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Uṣas
translation.summary: Now give we praise to Dadhikrâs the rapid, and mention in our laud the Earth and Heaven.
verses: Now give we praise to Dadhikrâs the rapid, and mention in our laud the Earth and Heaven. May the Dawns flushing move me to exertion, and bear me safely over every trouble.
I praise the mighty Steed who fills my spirit, the Stallion Dadhikrâvan rich in bounties, Whom, swift of foot aind shining bright as Agni, ye, Varuṇa and Mitra, gave to Pûrus.
Him who hath honoured, when the flame is kindled at break of dawn, the Courser Dadhikrâvan, Him, of one mind with Varuṇa and Mitra may Aditi make free from all transgression.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 39 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Agni
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: LET us recite the praise of Dadhikrâvan: may all the Mornings move me to exertion; Praise of the Lord of Waters, Dawn, and Agni, Br̥ihaspati Son of Angiras, and Sûrya.

Brave, seeking war and booty, dwelling with the good and with the swift, may he hasten the food of Dawn. May he the true, the fleet, the lover of the course, the bird-like Dadhikrâvan, bring food, strength, and light.
His pinion, rapid runner, fans him m his way, as of a bird that hastens onward to its aim, And, as it were a falcon's gliding through the air, strikes Dadhikrâvan's side as he speeds on with might.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 40 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Indra
translation.summary: What laud, O Indra-Varuṇa, with oblation, hath like the Immortal Priest obtained your favour.
verses: WHAT laud, O Indra-Varuṇa, with oblation, hath like the Immortal Priest obtained your favour? Hath our effectual laud, addressed with homage, touched you, O Indra-Varuṇa, in spirit?
He who with dainty food hath won you, Indra and Varuṇa, Gods, as his allies to friendship, Jayeth the Vr̥itras and his foes in battles, and through your mighty favours is made famous.
Indra and Varuṇa are most liberal givers of treasure to the men who toil to serve them, When they, as Friends inclined to friendship, honoured with dainty food, delight in flowing Soma.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 41 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Varuṇa
translation.summary: I Am the royal Ruler, mine is empire, as mine who sway all life are all Immortals. Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow.
verses: I AM the royal Ruler, mine is empire, as mine who sway all life are all Immortals. Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow. I am the King of men's most lofty cover.
I am King Varuṇa. To me were given these first existinghigh celestial powers. Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow. I am the King of men's most lofty cover.
I Varuṇa am Indra: in their greatness, these the two wide deep fairly-fashioned regions, These the two world-halves have I, even as Tvashṭar knowing all beings, joined and held together.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 42 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 4.43
translation.summary: Who will hear, who of those who merit worship, which of all Gods take pleasure in our homage.
verses: WHO will hear, who of those who merit worship, which of all Gods take pleasure in our homage? On whose heart shall we lay this laud celestial, rich with fair offerings, dearest to Immortals?
Who will be gracious? Who will come most uickly of all the Gods? Who will bring liss most largely? What car do they call swift with rapid coursers? That which the Daughter of the Sun elected.
So many days do ye come swiftly hither, as Indra to give help in stress of battle. Descended from the sky, divine, strong-pinioned, by which of all your powers are ye most mighty?
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 43 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Aśvins
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Aśvins.
verses: WE will invoke this day your car, farspreading, O Aṣvins, even the gathering, of the sunlight,– Car praised in hymns, most ample, rich in treasure, fitted with seats, the car that beareth Sûrya.
Aṣvins, ye gained that glory by your Godhead, ye Sons of Heaven, by your own might and power. Food followeth close upon your bright appearing when stately horses in your chariot draw you.
Who bringeth you to-day for help with offered oblation, or with hymns to drink the juices? Who, for the sacrifice's ancient lover, turneth you hither, Aṣvins, offering homage?
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 44 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Yonder goes up that light: your chariot is yoked that travels rou
translation.summary: Yonder goes up that light: your chariot is yoked that travels round upon the summit of this heaven.
verses: YONDER goes up that light: your chariot is yoked that travels round upon the summit of this heaven. Within this car are stored three kindred shares of food, and a skin filled with meath is rustling as the fourth.

Forth come your viands rich with store of pleasant meath, and cars and horses at the flushing of the dawn, Stripping the covering from the surrounded gloom, and spreading through mid-air bright radiance like the Sun.

Drink of the meath with lips accustomed to the draught; harness for the meath's sake the chariot that ye love. Refresh the way ye go, refresh the paths with meath: hither, O Aṣvins, bring the skin that holds the meath.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 45 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Prayer to Vāyu
translation.summary: Drink the best draught of Soma-juice, O Vâyu, at our holy rites: For thou art he who drinketh first..
verses: DRINK the best draught of Soma-juice, O Vâyu, at our holy rites: For thou art he who drinketh first.
Come, team-drawn, with thy hundred helps, with Indra, seated in the car, Vaya, and drink your fill of juice.
May steeds a thousand bring you both, Indra. and Vâyu, hitherward To drink the Soma, to the feagt.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 46 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Vāyu's Brilliance
translation.summary: Vâyu, the bright is offered thee, best of the meath at holy rites. Come thou to drink the Soma juice, God, longed-for, on thy team-drawn car..
verses: Vâyu, the bright is offered thee, best of the meath at holy rites. Come thou to drink the Soma juice, God, longed-for, on thy team-drawn car.
O Vâyu, thou and Indra are meet drinkers of these Soma-draughts, For unto you the drops proceed as waters gather to the vale.
O Indra-Vâyu, mighty Twain, speeding together, Lords of Strength, Come to our succour with your team, that ye may drink the Soma juice.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 47 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Vāyu the Bestower of Wealth
translation.summary: Taste offerings never tasted yet, as bards enjoy the foeman's wealth. O Vâyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice..
verses: TASTE offerings never tasted yet, as bards enjoy the foeman's wealth. O Vâyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.
Removing curses, drawn by teams, with Indra, seated by thy side, O Vâyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.
The two dark treasuries of wealth that wear all beauties wait on thee. O Vâyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 48 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Indra
translation.summary: Dear is this offering in your mouth, O Indra and Br̥ihaspati: Famed is the laud, the gladdening draught..
verses: DEAR is this offering in your mouth, O Indra and Br̥ihaspati: Famed is the laud, the gladdening draught.
This lovely Soma is effused, O Indra and Br̥ihaspati, For you, to drink it and rejoice.
As Soma-drinkers to our house come, Indra and Br̥ihaspati-and Indra-to drink Soma juice.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 49 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Bṛhaspati
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Bṛhaspati.
verses: Him who with might hath propped earth's ends, who sitteth in threefold seat, Br̥ihaspati, with thunder, Him of the pleasant tongue have ancient sages, deep-thinking, holy singers, set before them.
Wild in their course, in well-marked wise rejoicing were they, Br̥ihaspati, who pressed around us. Preserve Br̥ihaspati, the stall uninjured, this company's raining, ever-moving birthplace.
Br̥ihaspati, from thy remotest distance have they sat down who love the law eternal. For thee were dug wells springing from the mountain, which murmuring round about pour streams of sweetness.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 50 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Forth from the darkness in the region eastward this most abundant
translation.summary: Forth from the darkness in the region eastward this most abundant splendid light hath mounted.
verses: FORTH from the darkness in the region eastward this most abundant splendid light hath mounted. Now verily the far-refulgent Mornings, Daughters of Heaven, bring welfare to the people.
The richly-coloured Dawns have mounted eastward, like pillars planted at our sacrifices, And, flushing far, splendid and purifying, unbarred the portals of the fold of darkness.
Dispelling gloom this day the wealthy Mornings urge liberal givers to present their treasures. In the unlightened depth of darkness round them let niggard traffickers sleep unawakened.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 51 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 4.52
translation.summary: This Lady, giver of delight, after her Sister shining forth, Daughter of Heaven, hath shown herself.-.
verses: THIS Lady, giver of delight, after her Sister shining forth, Daughter of Heaven, hath shown herself.-
Unfailing, Mother of the Kine, in colour like a bright red mare, The Dawn became the Aṣvins' Friend.
Yea, and thou art the Aṣvins' Friend, the Mother of the Kine art thou: O Dawn thou rulest over wealth.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 52 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Savitṛ the Divine
translation.summary: Of Savitar the God, the sapient Asura, we crave this great gift which is worthy of our choice, Wherewith he freely grants his worshiper defence.
verses: OF Savitar the God, the sapient Asura, we crave this great gift which is worthy of our choice, Wherewith he freely grants his worshiper defence. This with his rays the Great God hath vouchsafed to us.

Sustainer of the heaven, Lord of the whole world's life, the Sage, he putteth on his golden-coloured mail. Clear-sighted, spreading far, filling the spacious realm, Savitar hath brought forth bliss that deserveth laud.

He hath filled full the regions of the heaven and earth: the God for his own strengthening waketh up the hymn. Savitar hath stretched out his arms to cherish life, producing with his rays and lulling all that moves.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 53 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Savitṛ
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Savitṛ.
verses: Now must we praise and honour Savitar the God: at this time of the day the men must call to him, Him who distributes wealth to Manu's progeny, that he may grant us here riches most excellent.
For thou at first producest for the holy Gods the noblest of all portions, immor-tality: Thereafter as a gift to men, O Savitar, thou openest existence, life succeeding life.

If we, men as we are, have sinned against the Gods through want of thought, in weakness, or through insolence, Absolve us from the guilt and make us free from sin, O Savitar, alike among both Gods and men.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 54 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacrifice to Varuṇa
translation.summary: Who of you, Vasus, saveth. who protecteth. O Heaven and Earth and Aditi, preserve us, Varuṇa., Mitra, from the stronger mortal.
verses: WHO of you, Vasus, saveth? who protecteth? O Heaven and Earth and Aditi, preserve us, Varuṇa., Mitra, from the stronger mortal. Gods, which of you at sacrifice giveth comfort?
They who with laud extol the ancient statutes, when they shine forth infallible dividers, Have ordered as perpetual Ordainers, and beamed as holy-thoughted WonderWorkers.
The Housewife Goddess, Aditi, and Sindhu, the Goddess Svasti I implore for friendship: And may the unobstructed Night and Morning both, day and night, provide for our protection.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 55 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: May mighty Heaven and Earth
translation.summary: A sacred hymn from the ancient Rigveda.
verses: MAY mighty Heaven and Earth, most meet for honour, be present here with light and gleaming splendours; When, fixing them apart, vast, most extensive, the Steer roars loudly in far-reaching courses.
The Goddesses with Gods, holy with holy, the Two stand pouring out their rain, exhaustless: Faithful and guileless, having Gods for children, leaders of sacrifice with shining splendours.
Sure in the worlds he was a skilful Craftsman, he who produced these Twain the Earth and Heaven. Wise, with his power he brought both realms, together spacious and deep, wellfashioned, unsupported.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 56 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Divine Steed
translation.summary: We through the Master of the Field, even as through a friend, obtain What nourisheth our kine and steeds. In such may he be good to us..
verses: WE through the Master of the Field, even as through a friend, obtain What nourisheth our kine and steeds. In such may he be good to us.
As the cow yieldeth milk, pour for us freely, Lord of the Field, the wave that beareth sweetness, Distilling meath, well-purified like butter, and let the. Lords of holy Law be gracious.
Sweet be the plants for us. the heavens, the waters, and full of sweets for us be air's mid-region. May the Field's Lord for us be full of sweetness, and may we follow after him uninjured.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 57 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Forth from the ocean sprang the wave of sweetness: together with
translation.summary: A sacred hymn from the ancient Rigveda.
verses: FORTH from the ocean sprang the wave of sweetness: together with the stalk it turned to Amrit, That which is holy oil's mysterious title: but the Gods' tongue is truly Amrit's centre.
Let us declare aloud the name of Ghr̥ita, and at this sacrifice hold it up with homage. So let the Brahman hear the praise we utter. This hath the four-horned Buffalo emitted.
Four are his horns, three are the feet that bear him; his heads are two, his hands are seven in number. Bound with a triple bond the Steer roars loudly: the mighty God hath entered in to mortals.
translation.context: From Mandala 4, Sukta 58 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni the Divine
translation.summary: Agni is wakened by the people's fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow.
verses: Agni is wakened by the people's fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow. Like young trees shooting up on high their branches, his flames are rising to the vault of heaven.
For worship of the Gods the Priest was wakened: at morning gracious Agni hath arisen. Kindled, his radiant might is made apparent, and the great Deity set free from darkness.
When he hath stirred the line of his attendants, with the pure milk pure Agni is anointed. The strength-bestowing gift is then made ready, which spread in front, with tongues, erect, he drinketh.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 1 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Youthful Mother keeps the Boy in secret pressed to her close
translation.summary: The youthful Mother keeps the Boy in secret pressed to her close, nor yields him to the Father.
verses: THE youthful Mother keeps the Boy in secret pressed to her close, nor yields him to the Father. But, when he lies upon the arm, the people see his unfading countenance before them.
What child is this thou carriest as handmaid, O Youthful One? The Consort-Queen hath bome him. The Babe unborn increased through many autumns. I saw him born what time his Mother bare him.
I saw him from afar gold-toothed, bright-coloured, hurling his weapons from his habitation, What time I gave him Amrit free from mixture. How can the Indraless, the hymnless harm me?
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 2 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Strength of Agni
translation.summary: Thou at thy birth art Varuṇa, O Agni; when thou art kindled thou becomest Mitra. In thee, O Son of Strength, all Gods are centred.
verses: THOU at thy birth art Varuṇa, O Agni; when thou art kindled thou becomest Mitra. In thee, O Son of Strength, all Gods are centred. Indra art thou to man who brings oblation.
Aryaman art thou as regardeth maidens mysterious, is thy name, O Self-sustainer. As a kind friend with streams of milk they balm thee what time thou makcst wife and lord oneminded.
The Maruts deck their beauty for thy glory, yea, Rudra! for thy birth fair, brightly-coloured. That which was fixed as Vishṇu's loftiest station-therewith the secret of the Cows thou guardest.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 3 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Wealth from Agni
translation.summary: O Agni, King and Lord of wealth and treasures, in thee is my delight at sacrifices.
verses: O AGNI, King and Lord of wealth and treasures, in thee is my delight at sacrifices. Through thee may we obtain the strength we long for, and overcome the fierce attacks of mortals.
Agni, Eternal Father, offering- bearer, fair to behold, far-reaching, far-refulgent, From well-kept household fire beam food to feed us, and measure out to us abundant glory.
The Sage of men, the Lord of human races, pure, purifying Agni, balmed with butter, Him the Omniscient as your Priest ye stablish: he wins among the Gods things worth the choosing.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 4 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Agni
translation.summary: To Agni, Jâtavedas, to the flame, the well-enkindled God, Offer thick sacrificial oil..
verses: To Agni, Jâtavedas, to the flame, the well-enkindled God, Offer thick sacrificial oil.
He, Narâṣansa, ne'er beguiled, inspiriteth this sacrifice: For sage is he, with sweets in hand.
Adored, O Agni, hither bring Indra the Wonderful, the Friend, On lightly-rolling car to aid.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 5 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Agni
translation.summary: I Value Agni that good Lord, the home to which the kine return: Whom fleet-foot coursers seek as home, and strong enduring steeds as home.
verses: I VALUE Agni that good Lord, the home to which the kine return: Whom fleet-foot coursers seek as home, and strong enduring steeds as home. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.
'Tis Agni whom we laud as good, to whom the milch-kine come in herds, To whom the chargers swift of foot, to whom our well-born princes come. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.
Agni the God of all mankind, gives, verily, a steed to man. Agni gives precious gear for wealth, treasure he gives when he is pleased. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 6 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Agni
translation.summary: Offer to Agni, O my friends, your seemly food, your seemly praise; To him supremest o'er the folk, the Son of Strength, the mighty Lord:.
verses: OFFER to Agni, O my friends, your seemly food, your seemly praise; To him supremest o'er the folk, the Son of Strength, the mighty Lord:
Him in whose presence, when they meet in full assembly, men rejoice; Even him whom worthy ones inflame, and living creatures bring to life.
When we present to him the food and sacrificial gifts of men, He by the might of splendour grasps the holy Ordinance's rein.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 7 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni the Mighty
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: O AGNI urged to strength, the men of old who loved the Law enkindled thee, the Ancient, for their aid, Thee very bright, and holy, nourisher of all, most excellent, the Friend and Master of the home.

Thee, Agni, men have stablished as their guest of old, as Master of the household, thee, with hair of flame; High-bannered, multiform, distributor of wealth, kind helper, good protector, drier of the floods.

The tribes of men praise thee, Agni, who knowest well burnt offerings, the Discerner, lavishest of wealth, Dwelling in secret, Blest One! visible to all, loud-roaring, skilled in worship, glorified with oil.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 8 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Offering to Agni
translation.summary: Bearing; oblations mortal men, O Agni, worship thee the God. I deem thee Jâtavedas: bear our offerings, thou, unceasingly..
verses: BEARING; oblations mortal men, O Agni, worship thee the God. I deem thee Jâtavedas: bear our offerings, thou, unceasingly.
In the man's home who offers gifts, where grass is trimmed, Agni is Priest, To whom all sacrifices come and strengthenings that win renown.
Whom, as an infant newly-born, the kindling-sticks have brought to life, Sustainer of the tribes of men, skilled in well-ordered sacrifice.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 9 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Wealth from Agni
translation.summary: Bring us most mighty splendour thou, Agni, resistless on thy way. With overflowing store of wealth mark out for us a path to strength..
verses: BRING us most mighty splendour thou, Agni, resistless on thy way. With overflowing store of wealth mark out for us a path to strength.
Ours art thou, wondrous Agni, bywisdom and bounteousness of power. The might of Asuras rests on thee, like Mitra worshipful in act.
Agni, increase our means of life, increase the house and home of these, The men, the princes who have won great riches through our hymns of praise.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 10 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni the Protector
translation.summary: The watchful Guardian of the people hath been born, Agni, the very strong, for fresh prosperity.
verses: THE watchful Guardian of the people hath been born, Agni, the very strong, for fresh prosperity. With oil upon his face, with high heaventouching flame, he shineth splendidly, pure, for the Bharatas.
Ensign of sacrifice, the earliest Household-Priest, the. men have kindled Agni in his threefold seat, With Indra and the Gods together on the grass let the wise Priest sit to complete the sacrifice.

Pure , unadorned, from thy two Mothers art thou born: thou camest fromVivasvan as a charming Sage. With oil they strengthened thee, O Agni, worshipped God: thy banner was the smoke that mounted to the sky.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 11 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Strength of Agni
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: To Agni, lofty Asura, meet for worship, Steer of eternal Law, my prayer I offer; I bring my song directed to the Mighty like pure oil for his mouth at sacrifices.
Mark the Law, thou who knowest, yea, observe it: send forth the full streams of eternal Order. I use no sorcery with might or falsehood the sacred Law of the Red Steer I follow.
How hast thou, follower of the Law eternal, become the knower of a new song, Agni? The God, the Guardian of the seasons, knows me: the Lord of him who won this wealth I know not.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 12 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Agni
translation.summary: With songs of praise we call on thee, we kindle thee with songs of praise, Agni, -with songs of praise, for help..
verses: WITH songs of praise we call on thee, we kindle thee with songs of praise, Agni, -with songs of praise, for help.
Eager for wealth, we meditate Agni's effectual praise to-day, Praise of the God who touches heaven.
May Agni, Priest among mankind, take pleasure in our songs of praise, And worship the Celestial Folk.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 13 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Agni
translation.summary: Enkindling the Immortal, wake Agni with song of praise: may he bear our oblations to the Gods..
verses: ENKINDLING the Immortal, wake Agni with song of praise: may he bear our oblations to the Gods.
At high solemnities mortal men glorify him the Immortal, best At sacrifice among mankind.
That he may bear their gifts to heaven, all glorify him Agni, God, With ladle that distilleth oil.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 14 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni's Treasures
translation.summary: To him, the far-renowned, the wise Ordainer, ancient and glorious, a song I offer.
verses: To him, the far-renowned, the wise Ordainer, ancient and glorious, a song I offer. Enthroned in oil, the Asura, bliss-giver, is Agni, firm support of noble, riches.
By holy Law they kept supporting Order, by help of sacrifice, in loftiest heaven,– They who attained with born men to the unborn, men seated on that stay, heaven's firm sustainer.
Averting woe, they labour hard to bring him, the ancient, plenteous food as power resistless. May he, born newly, conquer his assailants: round him they stand as round an angry lion.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 15 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Agni
translation.summary: Great power is in the beam of light, sing praise to, Agni, to the God Whom men have set in foremost place like Mitra with their eulogies..
verses: GREAT power is in the beam of light, sing praise to, Agni, to the God Whom men have set in foremost place like Mitra with their eulogies.
He by the splendour of his arms is Priest of every able man. Agni conveys oblation straight, and deals, as Bhaga deals, his boons.
All rests upon the laud and love of him the rich, high-flaming God, On whom, loud-roaring, men have laid great strength as on a faithful friend.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 16 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Invocation of Agni
translation.summary: God, may a mortal call the Strong hither, with solemn rites, to aid, A man call Agni to protect when sacrifice is well prepared..
verses: GOD, may a mortal call the Strong hither, with solemn rites, to aid, A man call Agni to protect when sacrifice is well prepared.
Near him thou seemest mightier still in native glory, set to hold Apart yon flame-hued vault of heaven, lovely beyond the thought of man.
Yea, this is by the light of him whom powerful siong hath bound to act, Whose bearns of splendour flash on high as though they sprang from heavenly seed.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 17 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Light of Agni
translation.summary: At dawn let: Agni, much-beloved guest of the house, be glorified; Immortal who delights in all oblations brought by mortal men..
verses: AT dawn let: Agni, much-beloved guest of the house, be glorified; Immortal who delights in all oblations brought by mortal men.
For Dvita who receives through wealth of native strength maimed offerings, Thy praiser even gains at once the Soma-drops, Immortal Gods!
Nobles, with song I call that car of yours that shines with lengthened life, For, God who givest steeds! that car hither and thither goes unharmed.
translation.context: From Mandala 5, Sukta 18 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.
