verses: SEE, Vena, born in light, hath driven hither, on chariot of the air, the Calves of Pr̥iṣni. Singers with hymns caress him as an infant there where the waters and the sunlight mingle.
Vena draws up his wave from out the ocean. mist-born, the fair one's back is made apparent, Brightly he shone aloft on Order's summit: the hosts sang glory to their common birthplace.
Full many, lowing to their joint-possession, dwelling together stood the Darling's Mothers. Ascending to the lofty height of Order, the bands of singers 'sip the sweets of Amrit.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 123 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni and the Sacrifice
translation.summary: Come to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions.
verses: COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions. Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness.
I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways, While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers.
I, looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order. I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 124 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

hymns.significance: Goddess Speech speaks in first person

translation.title: The Goddess Speech Speaks
translation.summary: Vac (Speech/Word) declares her own supremacy and creative power.
verses: I move with the Rudras, with the Vasus, with the Adityas and with all the gods.
I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those worthy of sacrifice.
Through me alone all beings eat food. Though they know it not, they dwell in me.
I, myself, speak forth what is welcome to gods and humans. Whom I love, I make mighty.
I breathe forth like the wind. Beyond heaven, beyond earth, so vast am I in my greatness.
translation.context: One of the most powerful feminist statements in ancient literature. Vac claims creative power, omnipresence, supremacy. Word/consciousness as ultimate reality.
translation.modernApplication: Celebrates feminine divine power, creative word, consciousness as fundamental. Understanding language's creative power.

translation.title: Mitra the Divine
translation.summary: No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man, Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes..
verses: No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man, Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes.
This very thing do we desire, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Whereby ye guhrd the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes.
These are, each one, our present helps, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 126 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Night
translation.summary: Celebrating night as protective, peaceful, and star-adorned.
verses: Night has come, looking around with her eyes. She has clothed herself in all her glories.
The immortal goddess has filled wide space. She drives away the darkness with her light.
So favor us this night, O you whose approach we welcome as cows welcome the dawn.
Ward off the she-wolf and the wolf. Ward off the thief. O Night full of waves, be easy for us to cross.
translation.context: Instead of fearing night, this hymn celebrates it as restful, protective, necessary. Night is personified as benevolent goddess.
translation.modernApplication: Helps overcome fear of darkness, validates rest and sleep, celebrates natural cycles.

translation.title: Agni the Victorious
translation.summary: Let me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies.
verses: LET me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies. May the four regions bend and bow before me: with thee for guardian may we win in combat.
May all the Gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts led by Indra, Vishṇu, Agni. Mine be the middle air's extended region, ani may the wind blow favouring these my wishes.
May the Gods grant me riches; may the blessing and invocation of the Gods assist me. Foremost in fight be the divine Invokers: may we, unwounded, have brave heroes round us.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 128 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

hymns.significance: THE NASADIYA SUKTA - Most famous philosophical hymn

translation.title: The Hymn of Creation (Nasadiya Sukta)
translation.summary: The ultimate philosophical inquiry into existence itself.
verses: Then was not non-existent nor existent: there was no realm of air, no sky beyond it.
Death was not then, nor was there aught immortal: no sign was there, the day's and night's divider.
Darkness there was: at first concealed in darkness, this All was indiscriminate chaos.
Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire, the primal seed and germ of Spirit.
Who verily knows and who can here declare it, whence it was born and whence comes this creation?
He, the first origin of this creation, whether he formed it all or did not form it, whose eye controls this world in highest heaven, he verily knows it, or perhaps he knows not.
translation.context: The most philosophically mature hymn. Instead of creation myth, it admits mystery. The final line—maybe even God doesn't know—is radical intellectual humility.
translation.modernApplication: Validates living with uncertainty, mystery, not-knowing. Relevant to existential questions, cosmology, consciousness studies.

translation.title: Sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side
translation.summary: A sacred hymn from the ancient Rigveda.
verses: THE sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side, stretched by a hundred sacred ministers and one,– This do these Fathers weave who hitherward are come: they sit beside the warp and cry, Weave forth, weave back.
The Man extends it and the Man unbinds it: even to this vault of heaven hath he outspun, it. These pegs are fastened to the seat of worship: they made the Sâma-hymns their weaving shuttles.
What were the rule, the order and the model? What were the wooden fender and the butter? What were the hymn, the chant, the recitation, when to the God all Deities paid worship?
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 130 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra's Power
translation.summary: Drive all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern.
verses: DRIVE all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern. Hero, drive off our northem foes and southem, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful.
What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order, So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who went not to prepare the grass for worship.
Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies. Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 131 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn of Praise to Aśvins
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Aśvins.
verses: MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice, And may the Aṣvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss.
As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk. So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends.
And when we seek to win your love and friendship, we.who have precious wealth in our possession, Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 132 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra the Mighty
translation.summary: Sing strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place.
verses: SING strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place. Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.

Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs. Thy bolt thou castest, at the foe, O Indra, who would srnite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 133 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Strength of Indra
translation.summary: As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven.
verses: As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven. So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.

Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness. Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies. With all thy powers, O Ṣakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down:
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 134 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: In the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with t
translation.summary: In the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods, The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires..
verses: IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods, The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires.
I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old, On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again.
Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less car Which thou hast fashioned mentally, onepoled but turning every way.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 135 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: The Long-Haired Ascetic
translation.summary: Describes wandering mystics with supernatural powers gained through austerity.
verses: The long-haired one endures fire, the long-haired one endures poison, the long-haired one endures both worlds.
The long-haired one is said to gaze upon all, he is said to be this light.
The ascetics, wearing wind as their belt and clad in soiled yellow robes, follow the wind's swift course.
We have mounted the winds; you mortals see only our bodies.
The ascetic drinks poison with Rudra from the cup.
translation.context: Earliest description of yogic ascetics (munis) in Vedic literature. Shows that renunciant tradition existed alongside ritual tradition.
translation.modernApplication: Connects to yoga, meditation, renunciation traditions. Validates paths of extreme austerity and mystical experience.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 10.137
translation.summary: Ye Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low. O Gods, restore to life again the man who hath committed sin..
verses: YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low. O Gods, restore to life again the man who hath committed sin.
Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land. May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away.
Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind; For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 137 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Prayer to Indra
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vr̥itra limb from limb, When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call.

Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath. Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law.
In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Ârya found a match to meet his Dam foe. Associate with R̥ijiṣvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 138 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Light of Sūrya
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Sūrya.
verses: SAVITAR, golden-haired, hath lifted eastward, bright With the sunbeams, his eternal lustre; He in whose energy wise Pûshan marches, surveying all existence like a herdsman.
Beholding men he sits amid the heaven filling the two world-halves and air's wide region. He looks upon the rich far-spreading pastures between the eastern and the western limit.
He, root of wealth, the gatherer-up of treasures, looks with his might on every form and figure. Savitar, like a God.whose Law is constant, stands in the battle for the spoil like Indra.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 139 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Agni
translation.summary: Agni, life-power and fame are thine: thy fires blaze mightily, thou rich in wealth of beams.
verses: AGNI, life-power and fame are thine: thy fires blaze mightily, thou rich in wealth of beams! Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper, with strength, the food that merits laud.
With brilliant, purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light. Thou, visiting both thy Mothers, aidest them as Son: thou joinest close the earth and heaven.
O Jâtavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice ihyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs. In thee are treasured various forms of strengthening food, born nobly and of wondrous help.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 140 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Wealth from Agni
translation.summary: Turn hither, Agni, speak to us: come to us with a gracious mind. Enrich us, Master of the house: thou art the Giver of our wealth..
verses: TURN hither, Agni, speak to us: come to us with a gracious mind. Enrich us, Master of the house: thou art the Giver of our wealth.
Let Aryaman vouchsafe us wealth, and Bhaga, and Br̥ihaspati. Let the Gods give their gifts, and let Sûnr̥itâ, Goddess, grant us wealth.
We call King Soma to our aid, and Agni with our songs and hymns, Âdityas, Vishṇu, Sûrya, and the Brahman Priest Br̥ihaspati.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 141 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Praise of Agni
translation.summary: With thee, O Agni, was this singer of the laud: he hath no other kinship, O thou Son of Strength. Thou givest blessed shelter with a triple guard.
verses: WITH thee, O Agni, was this singer of the laud: he hath no other kinship, O thou Son of Strength. Thou givest blessed shelter with a triple guard. Keep the destructive lightning far away from us.

Thy birth who seekest food is in the falling flood, Agni: as Comrade thou winnest all living things. Our coursers and our songs shall be victorious: they of themselves advance like one who guards the herd.
And thou, O Agni, thou of Godlike nature, sparest the stones, while caring up the brushwood. Then are thy tracks like deserts in the corn-lands. Let us not stir to wrath thy mighty arrow.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 142 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Strength of Divine Steed
translation.summary: Ye made that Atri, worn with eld, free as a horse to win the goal. When ye restored to youth and strength Kakshîvân like a car renewed,.
verses: YE made that Atri, worn with eld, free as a horse to win the goal. When ye restored to youth and strength Kakshîvân like a car renewed,
Ye freed that Atri like a horse, and brought him newly-born to earth. Ye loosed him like a firm-tied knot which Gods unsoiled by dust had bound.
Heroes who showed most wondrous power to Atri, strive to win fair songs; For then, O Heroes of the sky, your hymn of praise shall cease no more.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 143 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Divine Steed
translation.summary: This deathless Indu, like a steed, strong and of full vitality, Belongs to thee, the Orderer..
verses: THIS deathless Indu, like a steed, strong and of full vitality, Belongs to thee, the Orderer.
Here, by us, for the worshipper, is the wise bolt that works with skill. It brings the bubbling beverage as a dexterous man brings the effectual strong drink.
Impetuous Ahîṣuva, a bull among cows of his, looked down upon the restless Hawk.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 144 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Out the earth I dig this plant
translation.summary: From out the earth I dig this plant, a herb of most effectual power, Wherewith one quells the rival wife and gains the husband for oneself..
verses: FROM out the earth I dig this plant, a herb of most effectual power, Wherewith one quells the rival wife and gains the husband for oneself.
Auspicious, with expanded leaves, sent by the Gods, victorious plant, Blow thou the rival wife away, and make my husband only mine.
Stronger am I, O Stronger One, yea, mightier than the mightier; And she who is my rival wife is lower than the lowest dames.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 145 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Goddess of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight
translation.summary: Goddess of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight. How is it that thou seekest not the village. Art thou not afraid?.
verses: GODDESS of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight. How is it that thou seekest not the village? Art thou not afraid?
What time the grasshopper replies and swells the shrill cicala's voice, Seeming to sound with tinkling bells, the Lady of the Wood exults.
And, yonder, cattle seem to graze, what seems a dwelling-place appears: Or else at eve the Lady of the Forest seems to free the wains.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 146 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra the Divine
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Indra.
verses: I TRUST in thy first wrathful deed, O Indra, when thou slewest Vr̥itra and didst work to profit man; What time the two world-halves fell short of thee in might, and the earth trembled at thy force, O Thunder-anned.
Thou with thy magic powers didst rend the conjurer Vr̥itra, O Blameless One, with heart that longed for fame. Heroes elect thee when they battle for the prey, thee in all sacrifices worthy of renown.

God Much-invoked, take pleasure in these princes here, who, thine exalters, Maghavan, have come to wealth. In synods, when the rite succeeds, they hymn the Strong for sons and progeny and riches undisturbed.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 147 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Indra
translation.summary: When we have pressed the juice we laud thee, Indra, and when, Most Valorous we have won the booty.
verses: WHEN we have pressed the juice we laud thee, Indra, and when, Most Valorous we have won the booty. Bring us prosperity, as each desires it under thine own protection may we conquer.
Sublime from birth, mayst thou O Indra, Hero, with Sûrya overcome the Dâsa races. As by a fountain's side, we bring the Soma that lay concealed, close-hidden in the waters.
Answer the votary's hymns, for these thou knowest, craving the R̥ishis' prayer, thyself a Singer May we be they who take delight in Somas: these with sweet food for thee, O Chariot-rider.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 148 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Savitṛ's Blessings
translation.summary: Savitar fixed the earth with bands to bind it, and made heaven stedfast where no prop supported.
verses: SAVITAR fixed the earth with bands to bind it, and made heaven stedfast where no prop supported. Savitar milked, as 'twere a restless courser, air, sea bound fast to what no foot had trodden.
Well knoweth Savitar, O Child of Waters, where ocean, firmly fixt, o'erflowed its limit. Thence sprang the world, from that uprose the region: thence heaven spread out and the wide earth expanded.
Then, with a full crowd of Immortal Beings, this other realm came later, high and holy. First, verily, Savitar's strong-pinioned Eagle was born: and he obeys his law for ever.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 149 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Rudra's Blessings
translation.summary: Thou, bearer of oblations, though kindled, art kindled for the Gods. With the Âdityas, Rudras, Vasus, come to us: to show us favour come to us..
verses: THOU, bearer of oblations, though kindled, art kindled for the Gods. With the Âdityas, Rudras, Vasus, come to us: to show us favour come to us.
Come hither and accept with joy this sacrifice and hymn of ours. O kindled God, we mortals are invoking thee, calling on thee to show us grace.
I laud thee Jâtavedas, thee Lord of all blessings, with my song. Agni, bring hitherward the Gods whose Laws we love, whose laws we love, to show us grace.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 150 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Agni
translation.summary: By Faith is Agni kindled, through Faith is oblation offered up. We celebrate with praises Faith upon the height of happiness..
verses: By Faith is Agni kindled, through Faith is oblation offered up. We celebrate with praises Faith upon the height of happiness.
Bless thou the man who gives, O Faith; Faith, bless the man who fain would give. Bless thou the liberal worshippers: bless thou the word that I have said.
Even as the Deities maintained Faith in the mighty Asuras, So make this uttered wish of mine true for the liberal worshippers.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 151 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Mighty Governor art thou
translation.summary: A Mighty Governor art thou, Wondrous, Destroyer of the foe, Whose friend is never done to death, and never, never overcome..
verses: A MIGHTY Governor art thou, Wondrous, Destroyer of the foe, Whose friend is never done to death, and never, never overcome.
Lord of the clan, who brings us bliss, Strong, Warrior, Slayer of the fiend, May India, Soma-drinker, go before us, Bull who gives us peace.
Drive Raksasas and foes away, break thou in pieces Vr̥itra'sjaws: O Vr̥itra-slaying Indra, quell the foeman's wrath who threatens us.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 152 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra's Blessings
translation.summary: Swaying about, the Active Ones came nigh to Indra at his birth, And shared his great heroic might..
verses: SWAYING about, the Active Ones came nigh to Indra at his birth, And shared his great heroic might.
Based upon strength and victory and power, O Indra is thy birth: Thou, Mighty One, art strong indeed.
Thou art the Vr̥itra-slayer, thou, Indra, hast spread the firmament: Thou hast with might upheld the heavens.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 153 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Soma's Blessings
translation.summary: For some is Soma purified, some sit by sacrificial oil: To those for whom the meath flows forth, even to those let him depart..
verses: FOR some is Soma purified, some sit by sacrificial oil: To those for whom the meath flows forth, even to those let him depart.
Invincible through Fervour, those whom Fervour hath advanced to heaven, Who showed great Fervour in their lives, -even to those let him depart.
The heroes who contend in war and boldly cast their lives away, Or who give guerdon thousandfold, -even to those let him depart.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 154 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 10.155
translation.summary: Arayi, one-eyed limping hag, fly, ever-screeching, to the hill. We frighten thee away with these, the heroes of Ṣirimbiṭha..
verses: ARAYI, one-eyed limping hag, fly, ever-screeching, to the hill. We frighten thee away with these, the heroes of Ṣirimbiṭha.
Scared from this place and that is she, destroyer of each germ unborn. Go, sharp-horned Brahmanaspti and drive Arayi far away.
Yon log that floats without a man to guide it on the river's edge,– Seize it, thou thing with hideous jaws, and go thou far away thereon.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 155 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Agni
translation.summary: Let songs of ours speed Agni forth like a fleet courser in the race, And we will win each prize through him..
verses: LET songs of ours speed Agni forth like a fleet courser in the race, And we will win each prize through him.
Agni the dart whereby we gain kine for ourselves with help from thee,– That send us for the gain of wealth.
O Agni, bring us wealth secure, vast wealth in horses and in kine: Oil thou the socket, turn the wheel.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 156 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Indra
translation.summary: We will, with Indra and all Gods to aid us, bring these existing worlds into subjection..
verses: WE will, with Indra and all Gods to aid us, bring these existing worlds into subjection.
Our sacrifice, our bodies, and our offspr. let Indra form together with Âdityas.
With the Âdityas, with the band of Maruts, may Indra be Protector of our bodies.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 157 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni the Protector
translation.summary: May Sûrya guard us out of heaven, and Vâta from the firmament, And Agni from terrestrial spots..
verses: MAY Sûrya guard us out of heaven, and Vâta from the firmament, And Agni from terrestrial spots.
Thou Savitar whose flame deserves hundred libations, be thou pleased: From failing lightning keep us safe.
May Savitar the God, and may Parvata also give us sight; May the Creator give us sight.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 158 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Victory through Sūrya
translation.summary: Yon Sun hath mounted up, and this my happy fate hate mounted high. I knowing this, as conqueror have won my husband for mine own..
verses: YON Sun hath mounted up, and this my happy fate hate mounted high. I knowing this, as conqueror have won my husband for mine own.
I am the banner and the head, a mighty arbitress am I: I am victorious, and my Lord shall be submissive to my will.
My Sons are slayers of the foe, my Daughter is a ruling Queen: I am victorious: o'er my Lord my song of triumph is supreme.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 159 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Offering to Indra
translation.summary: Taste this strong draught enriched with offered viands: with all thy chariot here unyoke thy Coursers.
verses: TASTE this strong draught enriched with offered viands: with all thy chariot here unyoke thy Coursers. Let not those other sacrificers stay thee, Indra: these juices shed for thee are ready.
Thine is the juice effused, thine are the juices yet to be pressed: our resonant songs invite thee. O Indra, pleased to-day with this libation, come, thou who knowest all and drink the Soma.
Whoso, devoted to the God, effuses Soma for him with yearning heart and spirit,– Never doth Indra give away his cattle: for him he makes the lovely Soma famous.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 160 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Prayer to Agni
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Agni.
verses: FOR life I set thee free by this oblation from the unknown decline and from Consumption; Or, if the grasping demon have possessed him, free him from her, O Indra, thou and Agni.
Be his days ended, be he now departed, be he brought very near to death already, Out of Destruction's lap again I bring him, save him for life to last a hundred autumns.
With hundred-eyed oblation, hundred-autumned, bringing a hundred lives, have I restored him, That Indra for a hundred years may lead him safe to the farther shore of all misfortune.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 161 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Agni's Blessings
translation.summary: May Agni, yielding to our prayer, the Raksas-slayer, drive away The malady of evil name that hath beset thy labouring womb..
verses: MAY Agni, yielding to our prayer, the Raksas-slayer, drive away The malady of evil name that hath beset thy labouring womb.
Agni, concurring in the prayer, drive off the eater of the flesh, The malady of evil name that hath attacked thy babe and womb.
That which destroys the sinking germ, the settled, moving embryo, That which will kill the babe at birth,even this will we drive far away.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 162 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Both thy nostrils
translation.summary: From both thy nostrils, from thine eyes, from both thine ears and from thy chin, Forth from thy head and brain and tongue I drive thy malady away..
verses: FROM both thy nostrils, from thine eyes, from both thine ears and from thy chin, Forth from thy head and brain and tongue I drive thy malady away.
From the neck-tendons and the neck, from the breast-bones and from the spine, From shoulders, upper, lower arms, I drive thy malady away.
From viscera and all within, forth from the rectum, from the heart, From kidneys, liver, and from spleen, I drive thy malady away.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 163 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 10.164
translation.summary: Avaunt, thou Master of the mind Depart, and vanish far away. Look on Destruction far from hence. The live man's mind is manifold..
verses: AVAUNT, thou Master of the mind Depart, and vanish far away. Look on Destruction far from hence. The live man's mind is manifold.
A happy boon do men elect, a mighty blessing they obtain. Bliss with Vaivasvata they see. The live man's mind seeks many a place.
If by address, by blame, by imprecation we have committed sin, awake or sleeping, All hateful acts of ours, all evil doings may Agni bear away to distant places.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 164 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacred Hymn 10.165
translation.summary: Gods, whatsoe'er the Dove came hither seeking, sent to us as the envoy of Destruction, For that let us sing hymns and make atonement.
verses: GODS, whatsoe'er the Dove came hither seeking, sent to us as the envoy of Destruction, For that let us sing hymns and make atonement. Well be it with our quadrupeds and bipeds.
Auspicious be the Dove that hath been sent us, a harmless bird, ye Gods, within our dwelling. May Agni, Sage, be pleased with our oblation, and may the Missile borne on wings avoid us.
Let not the Arrow that hath wings distract us: beside the fire-place, on the hearth it settles. May, it bring welfare to our men and cattle: here let the Dove, ye Gods, forbear to harm us.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 165 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Make me a bull among my peers
translation.summary: Make me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror: Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine.
verses: MAKE me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror: Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine
I am my rivals' slayer, like Indra unwounded and unhurt, And all these enemies of mine are vanquished and beneath my feet.
Here, verily, I bind you fast, as the two bow-ends with the string. Press down these men, O Lord of Speech, that they may humbly speak to me.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 166 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Wealth from Indra
translation.summary: This pleasant meath, O Indra, is effused for thee: thou art the ruling Lord of beaker and of juice.
verses: THIS pleasant meath, O Indra, is effused for thee: thou art the ruling Lord of beaker and of juice. Bestow upon us wealth with many hero sons: thou, having glowed with Fervour, wortnest heavenly light.
Let us call Ṣakra to libations here effused, winner of light who joyeth in the potent juice. Mark well this sacrifice of ours and come to us: we pray to Maghavan the Vanquisher of hosts.
By royal Soma's and by Varuṇa's decree, under Br̥ihaspati's and Anumati's guard, This day by thine authority, O Maghavan, Maker, Disposer thou! have I enjoyed the jars.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 167 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: The Wind's chariot
translation.summary: O The Wind's chariot, O its power and glory. Crashing it goes and hath a voice of thunder.
verses: O THE Wind's chariot, O its power and glory! Crashing it goes and hath a voice of thunder. It makes the regions red and touches heaven, and as it moves the dust of earth is scattered.
Along the traces of the Wind they hurry, they come to him as dames to an assembly. Borne on his car with these for his attendants, the God speeds forth, the universe's Monarch.
Travelling on the paths of air's midregion, no single day doth he take rest or slumber. Holy and earliest-born, Friend of fhe waters, where did he spring and from what region came he?
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 168 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Rudra
translation.summary: May the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices.
verses: MAY the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices. May they drink waters rich in life and fatness: to food that moves on feet be gracious, Rudra.
Like-coloured, various-hued, or single-coloured, whose names through sacrifice are known to Agni, Whom the Angirases produced by Fervour,vouchsafe to these, Parjanya, great protection.
Those who have offered to the Gods their bodies, whose varied forms are all well known to Soma,– Those grant us in our cattle-pen, O Indra, with their full streams of milk and plenteous offspring.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 169 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacrifice to Soma
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Soma.
verses: MAY the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled meath, giving the sacrifice's lord uninjured life; He who, wind-urged, in person guards our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shines o'er many a land.

Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens, He rose, a light, that kills Vr̥itras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes.

This light, the best of lights, supreme, all-conquering, winner of riches, is exalted with high laud. All-lighting, radiant, mighty as the Sun to see, he spreadeth wide unfailing victory and strength.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 170 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Invocation of Indra
translation.summary: For Iṭa's sake who pressed the juice, thou, Indra, didst protect his car, And hear the Soma-giver's call..
verses: FOR Iṭa's sake who pressed the juice, thou, Indra, didst protect his car, And hear the Soma-giver's call.
Thou from his skin hast borne the head of the swift-moving combatant, And sought the Soma-pourer's home.
Venya, that mortal man, hast thou, for Âstrabudhna the devout, O Indra, many a time set free.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 171 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: All thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow
translation.summary: With all thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow on thy path..
verses: WITH all thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow on thy path.
Come with kind thoughts, most liberal, rousing the warrior's hymn of praise, with bounteous ones,
As nourishers we tie the thread, and, liberal with our bounty, offer sacrifice.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 172 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Be with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable
translation.summary: Be with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable. Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away..
verses: BE with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable. Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away.
Be even here; fall not away be like a mountain unremoved. Stand stedfast here like Indra's self, and hold the kingship in the grasp.
This man hath Indra stablished, made secure by strong oblation's power. May Soma speak a benison, and Brahmaṇaspati, on him.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 173 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Offering to Indra
translation.summary: With offering for success in fight whence Indra was victorious. With this, O Brahmaṇaspati, let us attain to royal sway..
verses: WITH offering for success in fight whence Indra was victorious. With this, O Brahmaṇaspati, let us attain to royal sway.
Subduing those who rival us, subduing all malignities, Withstand the man who menaces, withstand the man who angers us.
Soma and Savitar the God have made thee a victorious King All elements have aided thee, to make thee general conqueror.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 174 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Savitṛ
translation.summary: May Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law: Be harnessed to the shafts, and press..
verses: MAY Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law: Be harnessed to the shafts, and press.
Stones, drive calamity away, drive ye away malevolence: Make ye the Cows our medicine.
Of one accord the upper Stones, giving the Bull his bull-like strength, Look down with pride on those below.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 175 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Glory to Sacred Cattle
translation.summary: With hymns of praise their sons have told aloud the R̥ibhus' mighty deeds. Who, all-supporting, have enjoyed the earth as, twere a mother cow..
verses: WITH hymns of praise their sons have told aloud the R̥ibhus' mighty deeds. Who, all-supporting, have enjoyed the earth as, twere a mother cow.
Bring forth the God with song divine, being Jâtavedas hitherward, To bear our gifts at once to heaven.
He here, a God-devoted Priest, led forward comes to sacrifice. Like a car covered for the road, he, glowing, knows, himself, the way.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 176 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned
translation.summary: The sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned with all an Asura's magic might.
verses: THE sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned with all an Asura's magic might. Sages observe him in the ocean's inmost depth: the wise disposers seek the station of his rays.
The flying Bird bears Speech within his spirit: erst the Gandharva in the womb pronounced it: And at the seat of sacrifice the sages cherish this radiant, heavenly-bright invention.
I saw the Herdsman, him who never resteth, approaching and departing on his pathways. He, clothed in gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 177 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: This very mighty one whom Gods commission
translation.summary: A sacred hymn from the ancient Rigveda.
verses: THIS very mighty one whom Gods commission, the Conqueror of cars, ever triumphant, Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Târkshya for our weal will we call hither.
As though we offered up our gifts to Indra, may we ascend. him as a ship. for safety. Like the two wide worlds, broad, deep far-extended, may we be safe both when he comes and leaves you.
He who with might the Five Lands hath pervaded, like Sûrya with his lustre, and the waters- His strength wins hundreds, thousands none avert it, as- the young maid repelleth not her lover.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 178 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Indra's Blessings
translation.summary: Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share. If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise..
verses: Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share. If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise.

Oblation is prepared: come to us, Indra; the Sun hath travelled over half his journey. Friends with their stores are sitting round thee waiting like lords of clans for the tribe's wandering chieftain.
Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well-dressed, I fancy, is this recent present. Drink, Indra, of the curd of noon's libation with favour, Thunderer, thou whose deeds are mighty.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 179 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Invocation of Indra
translation.summary: O Much-invoked, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty.
verses: O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty. In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches.
Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance. Whetting thy bold and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us.
Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o'er the people. Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 180 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Light of Viṣṇu
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Viṣṇu.
verses: Vasishṭha mastered the Rathantara, took it from radiant Dhatar, Savitar, and Vishṇu, Oblation, portion of fourfold oblation, known by the names of Saprathas and Prathas.
These sages found what lay remote and hidden, the sacrifice's loftiest secret essence. From radiant Dhatar, Savitar, and Vishṇu, from Agni, Bharadvâja brought the Br̥ihat.
They found with mental eyes the earliest Yajus, a pathway to the Gods, that had descended. From radiant Dhitar, Savitar, and Vishṇu, from Sûrya did these sages bring the Gharma.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 181 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Sacrifice to Bṛhaspati
translation.summary: A sacred hymn of devotion to Bṛhaspati.
verses: Br̥ihaspati lead us safely over troubless and turn his evil thought against the sinner; Repel the curse, and drive away ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and cornfort!
May Narâṣansa aid us at Prayâja: blest be our Anuyâja at invokings. May he repel the curse, and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
May he whose head is flaming burn the demons, haters of prayer, so that the arrow slay them. May he repel the curse and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 182 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: I Saw thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and
translation.summary: I Saw thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and hath thence developed.
verses: I SAW thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and hath thence developed. Bestowing offspring here, bestowing riches, spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
I saw thee pondering in thine heart, and praying that in due time thy body might be fruitful. Come as a youthful woman, rise to meet me: spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
In plants and herbs, in all existent beings I have deposited the germ of increase. All progeny on earth have I engendered, and sons in women who will be hereafter.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 183 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Viṣṇu's Blessings
translation.summary: May Vishṇu form and mould the womb, may Tvashṭar duly shape the forms, Prajâpati infuse the stream, and Dhatar lay the germ for thee..
verses: MAY Vishṇu form and mould the womb, may Tvashṭar duly shape the forms, Prajâpati infuse the stream, and Dhatar lay the germ for thee.
O Sinîvâlî, set the germ, set thou the germ, Sarasvatî: May the Twain Gods bestow the germ, the Aṣvins crowned with lotuses.
That which the Aṣvins Twain rub forth with the attrition-sticks of gold,– That germ of thine we invocate, that in the tenth month thou mayst bear.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 184 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Varuṇa
translation.summary: Great, unassailable must he the heavenly favour of' Three Gods, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman..
verses: GREAT, unassailable must he the heavenly favour of' Three Gods, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.
O'er these, neither at home nor yet abroad or pathways that are Strange, The evil-minded foe hath power
Nor over him,. the man on whom the Sons of Aditi bestow Eternal light that he may live.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 185 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Filling our hearts with health and joy
translation.summary: Filling our hearts with health and joy, may Vâta breathe his balm on us May he prolong our days of life..
verses: FILLING our hearts with health and joy, may Vâta breathe his balm on us May he prolong our days of life.
Thou art our Father, Vâta, yea, thou art a Brother and a friend, So give us strength that we may live.
The store of Amrit laid away yonder, O Vâta, in thine home,– Give us thereof that we may live.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 186 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Hymn to Agni
translation.summary: To Agni send I forth my song, to him the Bull of all the folk: So may he bear us past our foes..
verses: To Agni send I forth my song, to him the Bull of all the folk: So may he bear us past our foes.
Who from the distance far away shines brilliantly across the wastes: So may he bear us past our foes.
The Bull with brightly-gleaming flame who utterly consumes the fiends So may he bear us past our foes.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 187 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Divine Steed the Divine
translation.summary: Now send ye Jâtavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous Steed To seat him on our sacred grass..
verses: Now send ye Jâtavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous Steed To seat him on our sacred grass.
I raise the lofty eulogy of Jâtavedas, raining boons, With sages for his hero band.
With flames of Jâtavedas which carry oblation to the Gods, May he promote our sacrifice.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 188 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: This spotted Bull hath come
translation.summary: This spotted Bull hath come, and sat before the Mother in the east, Advancing to his Father heaven..
verses: THIS spotted Bull hath come, and sat before the Mother in the east, Advancing to his Father heaven.
Expiring when he draws his breath, she moves along the lucid spheres: The Bull shines out through all the sky.
Song is bestowed upon the Bird: it rules supreme through thirty realms Throughout the days at break of morn.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 189 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

translation.title: Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Th
translation.summary: From Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose..
verses: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
From that same billowy flood of sea the Year was afterwards produced, Ordainer of the days nights, Lord over all who close the eye.
Dhatar, the great Creator, then formed in due order Sun and Moon. He formed in order Heaven and Earth, the regions of the air, and light.
translation.context: From Mandala 10, Sukta 190 of the Rigveda.
translation.modernApplication: Timeless Vedic wisdom for spiritual growth.

hymns.significance: FINAL HYMN OF RIGVEDA - Unity and Harmony

translation.title: Prayer for Unity
translation.summary: The concluding hymn of the Rigveda prays for collective harmony.
verses: Assemble together, speak together, let your minds be of one accord.
Common be your purpose, common be your heart, common be your intention, common be your mind, so that there may be thorough union among you.
Common be your prayer, common be your acquisition, common be your resolution, common your thought, and common your heart.
I make your purpose common, and your hearts of one accord. May your minds be as one and your souls as one, so you may live together in happiness.
translation.context: The perfect ending for the Rigveda. After thousands of verses exploring gods, sacrifice, philosophy, it concludes with human unity and harmony.
translation.modernApplication: Incredibly relevant for modern times. Calls for collective unity, shared purpose, harmony despite differences. Universal message.
